note: Seed data generated from the prototype's built-in checklist (checklistVersion 13). Same shape as the app's Management → Data & Access → Export backup.

items.text: All rostered staff are in
All staff arrived on time (at least 5 minutes before the session)
Absent staff have been chased up
items.guide: N/A if all rostered staff are present.

items.text: Staff presentation professional — dress, grooming and tidiness
dos: Smart or smart-casual and clean
Appropriate for working with children
ID / lanyard visible
donts: Scruffy, dirty or overly casual dress
Anything unsuitable for a children's setting

items.text: Non-tutor staff conduct professional — interactions with students, parents and colleagues
items.guide: Calm, respectful and professional with everyone on site.

items.text: Tutor conduct professional — behaviour with students and colleagues
dos: Tutors focused on teaching and their students
Any parent questions passed to a supervisor or admin
donts: Tutors speaking to parents at any point — this is not their role
Discussing a student's progress directly with a parent

items.text: Lanyards worn — blue for tutors, black for all other staff
ID cards complete — recent photo, full name and position
items.guide: Every member of staff on shift has a complete, current ID card.

items.text: Supervisor greeting parents before the session begins
Supervisor organised the class and teachers within the first 5 minutes
Expected students not yet in — how many absent?
items.guide: A record only — students can be absent for many reasons and that is not a mark against the centre. What matters is the follow-up below: any unexplained absence must be chased with parents.

items.text: All students arrived on time
Register taken on time (within 30 minutes of session start)
Parents contacted when a student has not shown up and the reason is unknown
items.guide: If an expected student is absent and the parent has not told us why, they must be called straight after the register so the parent is made aware. Not knowing where a child is is a serious safeguarding matter. Record who was called in the note. N/A only if every absence was already accounted for.

items.text: Correct staff-to-student ratios maintained
items.guide: Maximum 5 students per teacher. Record the actual ratio in the note if it exceeds this — a shortfall is a serious finding.

items.text: Admin available at front desk to accept late parents and secure the front entrance
dos: Admin at or near the front desk throughout the session
Late parents received and signed in
Front entrance supervised and kept secure
donts: Vulnerable students able to walk out the front unseen
items.guide: N/A only if the front entrance genuinely cannot be secured at this site.

items.text: How many toilet passes are available?

small.text: Small centre: 1 pass per gender (2 total).

medium.text: Medium centre: 2–3 passes per gender (4–6 total).

items.guide: Count the passes available and compare with the target for this centre size (set the size on the start screen). If there are fewer than the target, this is flagged for improvement.

items.text: Toilet passes given out by the supervisor or teaching assistant (not taken freely)
items.guide: Passes should be handed out and controlled by the supervisor or teaching assistant, so no student is wandering the centre without reason.

items.text: Difficult students dealt with appropriately
dos: Calm, fair and consistent approach
Clear expectations reset with the student
Escalated to a supervisor where needed
donts: Shouting at or publicly humiliating a student
items.guide: Record the teacher's name, then note the situation, the approach used and whether it was effective. N/A if no difficult behaviour was seen.

items.text: Classroom noise managed effectively
dos: A low, productive working hum — talk is about the work
Off-task chatter redirected quickly and calmly
Room settles again within moments of a prompt
donts: Shouting across the room to be heard
Students unable to concentrate because of the noise
items.guide: Well-managed noise is a productive working level, not silence. “Too much disruption” = learning is being disrupted.

items.text: Teaching pitched at the right level for each student
items.guide: Work is neither too easy nor too hard; tutors adapt to the student in front of them.

items.text: Tutors marking work and giving feedback during the session
Students' progress checked against their targets
items.guide: Tutors know each student's targets and are checking work against them, not just marking in isolation.

items.text: Session follows the planned curriculum / GoTutors materials
items.guide: Follows the GoTutors curriculum and materials. Note: students preparing for exams may skip ahead or leave out topics in the book to focus on what is coming up in their exams — that is expected, not a deviation.

items.text: Tutor–student interaction positive and encouraging
dos: Praises effort, not just correct answers
Keeps struggling students feeling capable and supported
Patient, warm and encouraging tone
donts: Making a student feel they are not smart enough
items.guide: Tutors should keep students feeling positive about the work even when they are struggling — never make a student feel they aren’t good enough.

items.text: Books reviewed this visit
items.guide: Sample a spread of books across different abilities — aim for at least 3.

items.text: Work is marked and up to date
items.guide: Recent work is marked; the book isn't full of unmarked pages.

items.text: Marking gives useful feedback, not just ticks
dos: Comments show the student what to fix
Next steps or targets noted
Errors clearly identified
donts: Whole pages left with no comment

items.text: Working / worked solutions shown and marked, not just final answers
items.guide: Mainly for Maths and Science — the method is shown and marked, not only the answer. N/A for essay-based work.
dos: Full method or working visible
Method marked, not just the final answer
donts: Working done on scrap and thrown away

items.text: Work and worked solutions neatly stapled / organised in the book
dos: Loose sheets stapled or stuck in, in order
Book is easy to follow
donts: Work out of order or missing

items.text: Homework set and marked
items.guide: Homework is being set and then actually marked and returned. N/A if homework isn't part of this student's plan.

items.text: Students act on feedback — corrections and improvements are done
items.guide: There's evidence students go back and correct or improve flagged work, not just receive it.

items.text: Tutor spots when a student needs help without being asked
items.guide: Record the tutor observed. Reads the room and steps in before a hand goes up. If no Maths lesson was observed this visit, mark this whole section N/A.
dos: Scans the class and steps in early
Notices body language or a stalled student
donts: Only helps when a hand goes up

items.text: Tutor pinpoints where in the problem the student is stuck
items.guide: Finds the exact step the student doesn't understand rather than re-teaching the whole thing.

items.text: Tutor identifies further weaknesses and scaffolds understanding
dos: Breaks the problem into steps
Addresses the root gap, not just the symptom
donts: Gives the answer and moves on

items.text: Tutor gives clear examples, then further examples to solidify understanding
dos: Models a worked example first
Follows up with practice examples
donts: Explains verbally with nothing written down
One example then moves on too soon

items.text: Tutor demands worked-out solutions from the student, not just answers
items.guide: Expects the student to show their method, and marks the method — not only the final answer.

items.text: Tutor prompts the student toward the answer or next step, rather than giving it
dos: Asks a guiding question
Nudges the next step
donts: Takes the pen and does it for them

items.text: Tutor checks understanding after each step, not just at the end
items.guide: Confirms the student follows each step of the solution before moving on.

items.text: Tutor prepares students for unit tests with extra practice and verbal checks
items.guide: Uses further practice and quick verbal questions to confirm readiness before a unit test.

items.text: Tutor encourages the student, even for small wins
dos: Praises effort and progress
Keeps a positive tone

items.text: Tutor knows the English curriculum and how students are assessed
items.guide: Record the tutor observed. Confident with the specification and assessment objectives. If no English lesson was observed this visit, mark this whole section N/A.

items.text: Tutor has confident SPaG knowledge and explains the rules simply
dos: Explains the rule in plain terms
Gives a quick example of the rule
donts: Vague or shaky on the rule

items.text: Tutor uses accurate subject terminology and spots what the student uses or needs
items.guide: Correct terminology, and can identify techniques a student has used and which they should use to improve.

items.text: Tutor identifies the student's weaknesses and knows how to improve them
Tutor tailors explanations to the student's age and level
items.guide: Pitches language and depth to the individual student.

items.text: Tutor always gives examples when explaining
dos: Backs every explanation with an example
Uses model sentences or quotes

items.text: Tutor models answers for the student
items.guide: Shows what a good answer looks like, not just describes it.

items.text: Tutor identifies techniques and methods easily
Tutor prompts and leads the student with questions
dos: Asks guiding questions
Leads the student to the point

items.text: Tutor can simplify an explanation to match the student's needs
items.guide: Can strip an explanation right back without losing the point when a student needs it.

items.text: Tutor's teaching style is engaging
Tutor gives detailed, effective feedback
dos: Specific, actionable feedback
Student knows exactly how to improve

items.text: Tutor uses mark-scheme vocabulary
items.guide: Record the tutor observed. Uses the words the mark scheme rewards. If no Science lesson was observed this visit, mark this whole section N/A.

items.text: Tutor explains command words
items.guide: Makes clear what “describe”, “explain”, “evaluate” and so on actually require.

items.text: Tutor explains concepts correctly
Tutor encourages effort
Tutor builds the student's confidence
Tutor is patient
Tutor gives the student time to ask questions and explain concepts back
dos: Pauses for questions
Asks the student to explain it back
Hears out a wrong answer before correcting
donts: Shuts down a wrong answer immediately

items.text: Tutor gives thinking time rather than answering too quickly
items.guide: Allows the student time to think instead of jumping straight in with the answer.

items.text: Tutor checks for understanding rather than talking at the student
dos: Regularly checks the student is following
Two-way dialogue

items.text: Tutor asks prompting questions
Student becomes less reliant on the tutor through the session
items.guide: By the end the student is working more independently than at the start.

items.text: All current staff added to Zenzap
All former employees removed from Zenzap
items.guide: N/A if no staff have left since the last visit.

items.text: All relevant staff added to the relevant group chats
All staff added to operations software (once available)
items.guide: N/A until the operations software is live for this centre.

items.text: Deals / customer journey being tracked correctly
No-shows being called back consistently
Leads being called back consistently
No customer payments pending more than 1 month
items.guide: Answer Yes if there are no payments outstanding beyond a month.

items.text: Enough books for the centre size

small.text: Small centre (up to 50): minimum 3 books per subject.

large.text: Large centre (150+): minimum 10 books per subject.

items.guide: Check against the target for this centre size. If stock is below target, the centre must place an order on the day or show proof an order has already been made.

items.text: Enough book tests for the centre size
items.guide: If short, place an order on the day or show proof an order has already been made.

items.text: Enough student admission forms for the centre size
Enough teacher admission forms for the centre size
Enough stationery — pencils (students), red pens (teachers), green pens (supervisors), black pens (admins & HOC)
Safeguarding policy in place and staff know the designated lead
items.guide: Ask a staff member who the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) is — they must be able to name them. Record who you asked in the note.

items.text: Staff DBS / vetting confirmed on the record register
items.guide: Every member of staff present must have a confirmed DBS on the register. Do NOT photograph DBS records — note the finding in writing instead (data protection).

items.text: Accident & incident log up to date
Safe arrival and collection procedures being followed
items.guide: No child leaves with an unauthorised adult; arrivals and collections are supervised and recorded. Note any gap in the procedure.

items.text: Fire exits clear and signage visible
items.guide: Exits unobstructed and signage visible. If an exit is blocked, take a photo as evidence.

items.text: Fire drill recorded within the last 3 months
items.guide: Check the fire log for a drill in the last 3 months. Note the date of the last recorded drill.

items.text: First aid kit stocked and in date
items.guide: Kit present, fully stocked and in date. Photograph any missing or expired items.

items.text: Risk assessments reviewed and current
Premises clean and well maintained
Learning areas safe and suitable for the age group
Temperature and ventilation comfortable
Warm water available in toilets
Toilets clean and hygienic
Hand soap available
Toilet paper stocked
Hand drying facilities available
Female sanitation provision available
Cleaning products available
Hand sanitiser available
Student asked how they find the sessions
items.guide: Speak to at least one student privately; note what they say in their own words. N/A only if no student could be spoken to.

items.text: Parent asked about progress and communication
items.guide: Speak to a parent at drop-off or collection; note their words. N/A if no parent was available.

items.text: No concerns raised by students or parents on site
Teacher stand-ups observed during the session
items.guide: Count each time a teacher stands up to circulate or address the class — more circulating generally means more active engagement. Use the tally bar at the top to keep count through the session.

items.text: Student distractions observed during the session — getting up, talking, messing around, not focusing, distracting others
items.guide: Tally each clear student distraction — getting up, talking, messing around, losing focus or distracting others. Fewer is better. Use the counter at the top to keep count through the session.
